---
Sunlight appears white but is actually made up of all the colors of the visible spectrum. When sunlight enters Earth's atmosphere, it collides with gas molecules and scatters in all directions, with shorter wavelengths (blue and violet) scattering far more than longer ones (red and orange) due to a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering. Although violet scatters even more than blue, our eyes are more sensitive to blue and some violet is absorbed in the upper atmosphere, so we perceive the sky as blue.
